positioning: Half a dog tall, twice a dog brave.
story: The Dachshund was built for a fight underground. German foresters wanted a dog that could follow a badger down its tunnel and not back out.

The name says so. Dachs is badger. Hund is dog. Every odd thing about the shape is on purpose. Short legs keep the nose near the ground. The long body fits the burrow. The big bark carries up through the earth.
There are two sizes and three coats. Smooth, long, and wire. Red, cream, black and tan, dapple, and more. Each coat type seems to bring its own temper.
The shape even named a meal. German immigrants sold sausages that looked like the breed. By most tellings, that is how America got the hot dog.
The personality is far larger than the dog. A Dachshund is brave to the point of nonsense, stubborn as a stain, and certain it is in charge. You do not own a Dachshund. You are assigned to one.
Look after that long back. Skip the big jumps and the long stairs. Offer a hand up and a ramp.
fblocks: Dachshund is German for badger dog, from Dachs, badger, and Hund, dog. The name is a job description.
Waldi, the first official Olympic mascot, Munich, 1972. Famous owners include Picasso, Andy Warhol, and E. B. White.
One breed, two sizes, three coats. The long back needs care. Too many stairs and big jumps are hard on it, so offer a hand up.
Red, cream, black and tan, chocolate and tan, blue, dapple, brindle, and piebald. Smooth, long, or wire.
Recognized by the AKC in 1885, among its earliest breeds. Bred to take on prey far heavier than itself.
days: A wicker basket, a sunny balcony, and a senior Dachshund who has claimed both.
Dachshund is German for badger dog. The name is a job description.
Waldi, a Dachshund, was the first official mascot in Olympic history. Munich, 1972.
Smooth, long, and wire coats share one breed. Each tends to have its own attitude.
Look at the stairs. Do the math. Ask for a lift. There is no shame in a ramp.
The hot dog is said to be named for the Dachshund. The sausage looked like the dog.
Two friends, one knitted blanket, and rain on the glass. Noses touching.
last_walk:
A paper lantern glows, and the canal is quiet.
A Dachshund is rarely quiet. But at dusk, on a towpath, it walks slow and long. Low to the ground, nose to the stones, it reads the day one last time. Then home, a blanket, and the end of a large little life.
